title: Weight-loss surgery
what: The surgeon makes the stomach smaller or changes the path food takes. You feel full on less food and gradually lose weight.
why: For severe obesity, especially with diabetes, high blood pressure, or joint problems, when diets have not helped.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 3 hours, with 2 to 4 days in hospital
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
Diabetes and all your diabetes medicines
Snoring and pauses in breathing during sleep

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: There are usually many tests before surgery: blood tests, an upper endoscopy, an ultrasound, and specialist visits. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Diet
prepare.text: A special diet is often prescribed for 1 to 3 weeks before. It shrinks the liver and makes surgery easier.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

bring: Things for a hospital stay of a few days
steps: On the day, you change, and an IV line is placed
Stockings or bandages are put on your legs to prevent clots
The surgeon works through a few small openings in the belly
The stomach is made smaller, or a bypass is created
The seams are checked for leaks, and the openings are stitched
feel: Pain at the openings, sometimes in the shoulder. You will get painkillers
You feel less hungry and fill up quickly
after: You usually start getting up and walking on the first day
Drink in small sips. Your diet moves in stages: liquids, purees, soft food
Vitamins are often needed for life. Your doctor will prescribe them
Regular follow-up with your doctor and dietitian matters
Pregnancy is usually advised no sooner than 12 to 18 months after
red_flags: Severe belly pain, a fast pulse, or fever
Black stools or vomiting blood: call emergency services
Calf pain, shortness of breath, or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: How much weight will I lose?
faq.a: It varies. Many people lose most of their excess weight in 1 to 2 years. Results last if you stick to the diet.

faq.q: Can I eat like before afterward?
faq.a: Portions will stay small for good. You will need to follow new eating rules.

faq.q: Will I need to take vitamins?
faq.a: Usually yes, often for life. They protect against anemia and bone problems.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Follow the clinic's diet. Eat and drink only until the time you were given.
